mainEntity.name: این همان بوم مدل کسب‌وکار است؟

acceptedAnswer.text: می‌توانیم از بوم برای نمایش استفاده کنیم، ولی خروجی اصلی نقشه فرضیات و معیار ادامه یا توقف است، چون بوم به‌تنهایی نمی‌گوید چه چیزی را آزمایش کنید.

mainEntity.name: Is this the Business Model Canvas?

acceptedAnswer.text: We can use the canvas to present it, but the main output is the assumption map and the kill/continue criteria, because a canvas alone does not tell you what to test.

mainEntity.name: داده زیادی نداریم؛ باز هم ممکن است؟

acceptedAnswer.text: بله. کمبود داده خودش یک یافته است: فرض‌های بدون داده بالای نقشه ریسک می‌نشینند و اول آزمایش می‌شوند.

mainEntity.name: We have little data; is it still possible?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Missing data is a finding in itself: assumptions without data go to the top of the risk map and are tested first.

mainEntity.name: آیا خروجی را می‌توانیم به سرمایه‌گذار نشان دهیم؟

acceptedAnswer.text: بله، مال شماست. فقط آن را پیش‌بینی معرفی نکنید؛ فرض‌ها کنار عددها نوشته شده‌اند.

mainEntity.name: Can we show the output to investors?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, it is yours. Just do not present it as a forecast; the assumptions are written next to the numbers.

blocks.html:
1. Home
  2. Services
  3. Business model design
Business model design
A model you can test: assumptions, revenue logic, and kill/continue criteria, not just a convincing pitch deck.
Problem

items: A business model can be convincing on a slide while nobody knows which assumption, if wrong, breaks the whole thing. Assumptions that are not written down are not tested, and the decision to continue or stop is left to feeling.

blocks.html: Who it is for

items: Founders who want to know, before building, which assumptions their revenue model stands on.
Businesses with revenue that do not know which part makes money and which does not.
Teams considering a big change (new pricing, a new market) who want to test it small first.

blocks.html: Who it is not for

items: If you want a pitch deck to raise money. This service's output can feed a pitch deck, but it is not one.
If you want a financial forecast presented as a prediction. We build the calculation from your inputs and written assumptions, not a number that promises the future.
If you need investment, legal or tax advice. This service is none of those.

blocks.html: Approach

items: Diagnosis. Input: conversations with the founders and any sales and cost data you have. Output: an assumption map ranked by risk (which assumption does most damage if wrong). Owner: dadmor with you.
Redesign. Input: the approved assumption map. Output: a redesigned model with revenue logic and a spreadsheet where every number links to a written assumption. Owner: dadmor; approval: you.

Validation. Input: the redesigned model. Output: a test plan for the three riskiest assumptions, with kill/continue criteria written before each test, and a results log. Running the tests: you; design and analysis: dadmor.

blocks.html: Deliverables
Scope and timeline factors

items: What changes the size of each phase: number of products or revenue streams, number of markets, and how much real data exists.
What you supply: access to sales and cost data (whatever exists), founders' time for conversations, and running the tests.
What delays projects: data that cannot be found, and a test started without criteria written in advance.

blocks.html: Effort band

items: A separate fixed proposal for each phase. You can start with Diagnosis only and decide afterwards.

blocks.html: A band is the rough size of the work, not a price and not a duration. A fixed price is set only after a scoping conversation, in a written proposal.
The band is a starting estimate; the scoping conversation may move it.
Limits and risks

items: Testing reduces risk but does not guarantee success. The result may say the current model does not work; that is a useful output too.
Spreadsheet numbers are calculations, not predictions. Each is as reliable as the assumption behind it.
Running the tests is on you; if they are not run, Validation remains a plan.
